Analysis: Hypothesis 1 stands out for its clear mechanistic endpoints by defining immunogenic cell death markers (calreticulin, ATP, and HMGB1) which facilitate a direct evaluation of immune activation, making it relatively more testable. Its approach of dual targeting (survivin suppression and modulation of epigenetic factors affecting exosomal non-coding RNAs) provides a novel way to synergize with PD-1 inhibition, and the pre-defined immunologic readouts enhance its experimental plausibility and focus on safety through controlled gene editing. While Hypothesis 2 also presents an innovative strategy by targeting AEG‐1 and combining epigenetic modulation with checkpoint blockade, it faces additional challenges concerning the complexity of nanoparticle design and a less clearly delineated mechanistic framework. Overall, Hypothesis 1 is slightly superior in terms of novelty (through its unique dual-target rationale), plausibility (with established markers of immunogenic cell death), testability (defined endpoints and measurable outcomes), and a comparatively streamlined safety profile.
